overview: Two states of the same bacterium, one metabolically dormant and extraordinarily resistant, the other actively growing.
genZNote: Endospore: bacteria in survival mode. Vegetative cell: bacteria living their best life.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A dormant, highly resistant structure formed by certain Gram-positive genera (e.g. Bacillus, Clostridium) to survive harsh conditions.
aspects.valueB: The normal, metabolically active, growing and dividing form of a bacterial cell.

aspects.label: Resistance to Environmental Stress
aspects.valueA: Extremely resistant to heat, desiccation, radiation, and many disinfectants due to dipicolinic acid and a thick keratin-like coat.
aspects.valueB: Susceptible to standard heat, drying, and disinfection methods.

aspects.label: Formation Trigger
aspects.valueA: Nutrient depletion or other unfavorable conditions trigger sporulation.
aspects.valueB: Formed by binary fission whenever conditions support growth.

aspects.label: Clinical/Laboratory Relevance
aspects.valueA: Survives standard autoclaving parameters unless proper time/temperature/pressure are met — used to validate sterilization (biological indicators).
aspects.valueB: The target of routine disinfection and most antibiotics, which generally act on active metabolic processes.
